analysis: Examined head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 37819-39530). This is a public synthetic test-vector fixture holding request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, block chain hashes) and token_ids for gpt-oss-20b cases (multi_system, nulls, reasoning_effort, response_text). Content is synthetic strings like 'Public followup.' and 'Nulls must disappear', with no secrets, credentials, keys or real consumer prompts. The patch excerpt shows the same file adding an additional_context {enable_thinking:false} template input to a Qwen-style vector and changing expected token counts and chain hashes. No runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption or routing logic changed. Relevant surfaces are the prompt-contract and prefix-cache chain hashing (T-041, TB-007). The fixtures are expected outputs only; the cache-key and hash derivation code is not in this batch. Template-input differences (additional_context carrying reasoning_effort) affect prompt_contract_id and cache block hashes, but the visible units show consistent contract IDs (a60ed9ae... for gpt-oss-20b), and nothing indicates cross-tenant cache-key weakening. Remaining uncertainty: the corresponding generator and verification code in the Swift provider and coordinator, and the other hunks of the file (lines ~3020-4004, 43739+, 52354+), were not supplied. I could not verify that the changed vectors match the implementation or that cache-scope derivation is unchanged. No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
